notes.decision: Translated 'her tail' taking ⲥⲉⲧ as Lyc. variant of Sah. ⲥⲁⲧ 'tail,' with 3sg fem possessive ⲡⲉϩ- (= Sah. ⲡⲉⲥ-). The fish-tail comparison and morphology context support this. ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ is left untranslated — the term resists clear identification (possibly a flat fish, leech, or specific body-part).

Translated 'five other vehicles' — ⲟⲭⲏⲙⲁ (Greek ὄχημα) is the standard Manichaean term for cosmic vehicles/chariots. The list of five (darkness, mire, [ⲃⲁⲉ], bitterness, burning) corresponds to the Manichaean schema of five worlds/elements of darkness, though not in the canonical order.
Translated 'measure of irons.' ⲡⲉ̄ⲓϣ probably = Lyc. ⲡⲱϣ 'measure, portion'; ⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ = 'irons' (pl.). The context is iron heated red-hot from fire as image of the burning element.
Translated 'of receiving-matter' — verbal compound ⲭⲓ ('receive') + ⲍⲩⲗⲏ ('matter'). The matter that receives forms is identified as the Enthymesis of Death — standard Manichaean cosmology.
Greek loanword ζωγραφεῖν 'to paint, depict.' Matter 'painted herself through the nature of the dark land' — i.e. she fashioned her own image using dark substance.

Translated 'the bronze and the lead' — ⲍⲁⲙⲧ̄ = Sah. ϩⲟⲙⲧ̄ 'bronze'; ⲡⲁⲉⲓⲛⲉ likely a Lyc. variant for a metal in the iron/bronze/lead/tin sequence. The point is that no metal is harder than the archonic body of matter.
ⲕⲟⲡⲓⲥ = Greek κοπίς 'cleaver, knife'; ⲁⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'at all/in the All' as adverbial intensifier. Translated 'no knife at all' — the archon's body is unsplittable by any iron tool.

Tentatively rendered 'concealment.' Coptic ϩⲱⲧⲡ ('set, conceal') and ϩⲱⲧⲃ ('slay') both fit the Lyc. spelling ⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ. Context favours 'concealment in speech of her members,' since Matter conceals her son and reveals him alternately (segments 19–21).
ⲍⲟⲙⲓⲗⲓⲁ = Greek ὁμιλία 'company, conversation.' ⲥⲉⲃⲉ taken as Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲃⲉ 'mockery, folly'; alternative reading 'wisdom' (Sah. ⲥⲁⲃⲉ) does not fit the negative cosmic register here.
Translated 'magics.' ⲍⲓⲕ = Lyc. ϩⲓⲕ 'magic, sorcery.' The contemporary magical arts are framed as mysteries belonging to the kingdom of darkness.
Idiom ϩⲱⲛ ⲉⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'command' (literally 'lay charge upon the hand of'). Translated 'I command you.' Speaker is the Apostle to his elect.
Translated 'receive teaching.' ⲥⲃⲱ rendered consistently as 'teaching' per terminology guideline.

Translated 'verdict ... cut off.' ⲁⲡⲟⲫⲁⲥⲓⲥ = formal sentence (Greek ἀπόφασις, per accumulated vocabulary); ϣⲱⲧⲥ̄ '(they) cut her off' uses the same root as ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'decree/cut' — preserving the dual force of legal pronouncement and severance.
